newsitem.title: USA: Newell $1.86 '97 EPS estimate "pretty good" - exec.
newsitem.headline: Newell $1.86 '97 EPS estimate "pretty good" - exec.

text.p: The director of investor relations of Newell Co said Wednesday that Wall Street analysts' consensus earnings estimates of $1.86 for 1997 and $2.13 for 1998 are "pretty good."
"Both of those numbers look pretty good to me at this point," the executive, Ross Porter, said in an interview after he spoke to the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts.

In his address to the analysts, Porter said that the diversified manufacturer and supplier of consumer products to retailers would expand its Rolodex brand name to other products that the company makes in order to boost sales. The company produces such items as card files and personal organizers.

"Leveraging it presents excellent growth opportunities," Porter said, but gave no details as to which other products might carry the Rolodex brand name. The Rolodex business unit was acquired on March 5 from Insilco Corp.

William Alldredge, Newell's vice president of finance, who also spoke to the analysts, said that the company, beginning next year, would emphasize expansion in Latin America, an area he described as the "single greatest opportunity to grow internationally."

Alldredge said a consulting firm was studying Latin America to determine which product lines and countries offered Newell the greatest opportunities. "Toward the end of the year we'll establish priorities," he said.
